title: UI preview workflow: concurrency group must be per-PR only for preview-relevant events, otherwise a unique run_id
answers: Why did an unrelated PR event (label change, edit, sync) cancel my running UI preview deployment?
Why do UI preview runs get cancelled when a PR is pushed to or labelled with something other than ui-preview?
Where is the concurrency group for the UI Preview workflow chosen?
How do I make a new PR event type not cancel in-flight preview builds?
body:
Path: .github/workflows/ui-preview.yml, workflow-level `concurrency` block (group expression). Decides which PR events can cancel each other's UI preview runs: pushes to master share one group, and PR events share a per-PR group only when the PR carries the `ui-preview` label.
Rule: The group expression is evaluated before any job `if:` runs, so job conditions cannot protect an in-flight preview. Keep the shared `<workflow>-<pr number>-preview` group only for events that are meaningful to the preview; any other event must fall back to `github.run_id` so it gets its own unique group and cannot cancel. Keep `cancel-in-progress: true` for the shared branch.
Symptom: A running UI preview build was cancelled, or a redundant preview deployment started, after an unrelated pull_request event (e.g. a label other than ui-preview was added) on the same PR.
Constraints: Applies to the ui-preview workflow's concurrency only. Adding a new trigger type to `on:` requires deciding which group it lands in. Does not change the job-level gating itself.
applies: UI Preview GitHub Actions workflow concurrency selection in .github/workflows/ui-preview.yml.
says: An in-progress interface preview deployment gets cancelled when someone adds an unrelated label.
Editing the pull request description or title aborts the running preview build.
Keep active preview builds running when non-preview pull request events occur.
Routine pull request updates cancel the preview before it finishes deploying.
Ensure running web preview deployments are only cancelled by newer relevant preview commits.
search: In .github/workflows/ui-preview.yml, the workflow-level concurrency group expression must only assign the shared per-PR group (<workflow>-<pr number>-preview with cancel-in-progress: true) to preview-relevant events, falling back to github.run_id for all other PR events. Because concurrency is evaluated before job-level if: conditions execute, assigning a unique run_id prevents unrelated pull request events (like non-preview labels or edits) from cancelling in-flight preview builds. This rule applies strictly to concurrency group selection in the UI preview workflow and does not alter the job-level gating.
